proofs.full_local_argument: All following calculations are local, not a transcription. First, for z=(x,y), w=(u,v), write a=||x-u|| and b=||y-v||. Each block difference of F is at most L(a+b), hence ||F(z)-F(w)||^2<=2L^2(a+b)^2<=4L^2(a^2+b^2). Thus F is 2L-Lipschitz. At an unconstrained differentiable saddle, both partial gradients vanish, so F(z*)=0. For any p=(u,v), strong convexity in x and strong concavity in y give <gradient_x f(u,v),u-x*> >= f(u,v)-f(x*,v)+(mu_x/2)||u-x*||^2 and -<gradient_y f(u,v),v-y*> >= f(u,y*)-f(u,v)+(mu_y/2)||v-y*||^2. Also strong convexity of f(.,y*) at its minimizer x* gives f(u,y*)>=f(x*,y*)+(mu_x/2)||u-x*||^2, while strong concavity of f(x*,.) at its maximizer y* gives f(x*,v)<=f(x*,y*)-(mu_y/2)||v-y*||^2. Summing yields <F(p),p-z*> >= mu_x||u-x*||^2+mu_y||v-y*||^2 >= mu||p-z*||^2. Strong convexity and L_x-smoothness in a nonzero x direction give mu_x<=L_x, by comparing strong gradient monotonicity with the Lipschitz bound; similarly mu_y<=L_y. Hence mu<=L. Now fix a step and write z=z_k, p=z-eta F(z), q=z-eta F(p), d=z-p, h=q-p. Since q-z=h-d, direct expansion gives ||q-z*||^2=||z-z*||^2-2eta<F(p),p-z*>+||q-z||^2-2eta<F(p),h>. Using eta F(p)=z-q=d-h, the last two terms equal ||d||^2+||h||^2. Since d=eta F(z) and h=eta(F(z)-F(p)), this is equivalently -||d||^2-||h||^2+2eta<F(z),h>. A more useful exact identity, obtained by substituting d=eta F(z), is ||q-z*||^2=||z-z*||^2-2eta<F(p),p-z*>-||d||^2+||h||^2. Indeed ||q-z||^2-2eta<F(p),h>=||h-d||^2-2<d-h,h>=||d||^2+3||h||^2-4<d,h> does not give the required identity and is not a proof step; the following direct expansion is the operative derivation: q-z=-eta F(p) and z-p=d imply ||q-z*||^2=||z-z*||^2-2eta<F(p),p-z*>-2eta<F(p),d>+eta^2||F(p)||^2=||z-z*||^2-2eta<F(p),p-z*>-||d||^2+||eta F(p)-d||^2. Since eta F(p)-d=-h, the desired exact identity follows. Consequently, by the saddle inequality and ||h||<=2eta L||d||, ||q-z*||^2<=||z-z*||^2-2eta mu||p-z*||^2+(4eta^2L^2-1)||d||^2. The elementary inequality ||z-z*||^2=||(p-z*)+d||^2<=2||p-z*||^2+2||d||^2 gives ||p-z*||^2>=||z-z*||^2/2-||d||^2. Therefore ||q-z*||^2<=(1-eta mu)||z-z*||^2+(4eta^2L^2+2eta mu-1)||d||^2. At eta=1/(8L), the residual coefficient is at most 1/16+1/4-1=-11/16, so it may be discarded. This proves the contraction with eta mu=1/(8 kappa). Induction gives r_N<=(1-1/(8 kappa))^N r_0. Since 1-t<=exp(-t) for t>=0, the exponential and integer-budget corollaries follow by solving exp(-N/(8 kappa))r_0<=epsilon. If r_0=0 then F(z*)=0 makes both predictor and next iterate equal z*. The recurrence has two joint-gradient queries per iteration, giving the stated query counts.

assumptions: f is continuously differentiable. For every y and all x,u, f(u,y)>=f(x,y)+<gradient_x f(x,y),u-x>+(mu_x/2)||u-x||^2 with mu_x>0. For every x and all y,v, f(x,v)<=f(x,y)+<gradient_y f(x,y),v-y>-(mu_y/2)||v-y||^2 with mu_y>0.
A saddle z* exists in the full Euclidean product space; no constraints or projections are present.

Uniformly for all arguments: ||gradient_x f(x_1,y)-gradient_x f(x_2,y)||<=L_x||x_1-x_2||; ||gradient_x f(x,y_1)-gradient_x f(x,y_2)||<=L_xy||y_1-y_2||; ||gradient_y f(x,y_1)-gradient_y f(x,y_2)||<=L_y||y_1-y_2||; ||gradient_y f(x_1,y)-gradient_y f(x_2,y)||<=L_yx||x_1-x_2||. The four constants are finite and nonnegative, and L=max{L_x,L_xy,L_y,L_yx}>0.
The recurrence uses exact joint gradients and eta=1/(8L). Assumption 3 is interpreted according to its explicit gradient_y prose with the displayed subscripts recorded separately.
statement.conclusion: r_{k+1}<=(1-1/(8 kappa))r_k for every k>=0. Thus r_N<=(1-1/(8 kappa))^N r_0<=exp(-N/(8 kappa))r_0. If r_0>0 and 0<epsilon<r_0, any integer N>=ceil(8 kappa log(r_0/epsilon)) suffices for r_N<=epsilon. If r_0=0, all iterates equal z*. Main Theorem 7 states the universal form 1-c/kappa with positive parameter-independent c; supplement Eq.(130) prints c=1/8. The iterated and accuracy bounds are local corollaries proved below.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let m,n be positive integers, f:R^m x R^n -> R, and use Euclidean norms and inner products. Let z*=(x*,y*) be a saddle: f(x*,y)<=f(x*,y*)<=f(x,y*) for every x,y. Put F(x,y)=(gradient_x f(x,y),-gradient_y f(x,y)), mu=min(mu_x,mu_y), kappa=L/mu and r_k=||z_k-z*||^2. Define p_k=z_k-eta F(z_k), z_{k+1}=z_k-eta F(p_k).
statement.parameter_domains: m,n>=1 integers; mu_x,mu_y>0; finite block Lipschitz constants as stated; 0<mu<=L and kappa>=1. For the accuracy corollary, 0<epsilon<r_0 when r_0>0; N is a nonnegative integer.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every function and constants satisfying these assumptions and every initial z_0 in R^m x R^n, the deterministic recurrence satisfies the bound for every integer k>=0. Consequently the iterated bound holds for every integer N>=0; there is no expectation or probability qualifier.
